Task 3.2 To deliver a conceptual design of the crystallization process, we first did a thorough literature review of various crystallization & separation technologies followed by discussions with industry experts and technology providers. These findings were incorporated together with the information gathered in subtask 3.1 to develop conceptual design centered around a block flow diagram and a stream table. The study gave an understanding of mass flow rates and stream composition across the proposed crystallization & separation process. It highlights the importance of the liquid separation efficiency to minimize the water content in the solid stream that is fed to the regeneration unit which adds a non-negligible thermal energy penalty and is thus to be considered in the cost optimization (capital and operating cost trade-off) of the integrated DAC technology. Task 4 The overall goal of this task is to test contactors and operating conditions to optimize the CO absorption 2 using Holocene’s aqueous amino acid solution to establish relation between the absorption rate and different operating levers such as air/solution flow rates, fan energy, pressure drop, and solution concentrations. It is of utmost priority to quantify the size of contactor and fan energy (or pressure drop) with respect to the total CO captured per unit time. Therefore, the success criteria were proposed in terms of capture efficiency, 2 absorption rate, and pressure drop. Sensitivity analysis of fluid and contactor properties was performed to identify critical parameters that can influence the CO absorption rate under different operating conditions using the reduced order model. The 2 study provided an understanding of a critical range of parameters such as packing volume, air/solution flowrates on the impact of absorption performance. Further, the contactor test was tested under different scenarios for identifying any operational failure. Different retrofitting and design iterations were implemented to operate the test rig without any leakage and operational failure. Experimental plans were proposed with the help of the reduced order model. We also learned that the liquid distribution and residence time measurements are as crucial as the absorption test to fully explore the mass-transfer characteristics in the contactor. The contactor was modified to assist the liquid distribution and residence time measurements. Absorption experiments were conducted to investigate the influence of air flow rate, liquid flow rate, 8 solution concentration, and packing volume. We observed a significant increase in CO absorption with an 2 increase in air flow rate whereas the liquid flow rate had marginal impact on the absorption. Higher molar concentration of solution can have higher capacity of CO absorption but the concentration can also change 2 the fluid properties and negatively affect the mass-transfer coefficient and reduce CO absorption. 2 In the modeling space, a method was developed for extracting overall mass-transfer coefficient from experimental data and validation of mass-transfer models.
